So for an assignment, I have to see how this Carnivore system "fits with current laws, actions, attitudes, or beliefs regarding accessing electronic evidence?" Its an outdated thing, but the practice is still in use obviously. This deals with mass surveillance, but the course is on computer forensics.

My textbook sums up Carnivore as a system that is installed at ISP facilities that monitor's all traffic moving through them. The catch was that the FBI needed court authorization to use the system. It was a filtering tool that "only gathered information that the court authorized." So it could gather email addresses, BUT it couldn't go as far as gathering personal information. It also couldn't gather specific packets.

[Here's the wiki article on Carnivore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnivore_(software))

I figured it would make this assignment more interesting if I asked actual people what they think of this rather than restating statistics. This isn't entirely about mass surveillance, but more about using this to collect evidence.

Knowing how this place was before I disappeared a few months ago, I'm assuming we all have similar opinions.

Thanks for reading! And thanks for helping!

Alright, suppose I'll hit this point-by-point.

Allow users to mute all replies from a tweet.

This sort of thing would obviously be used by people who don't like it when people reply to tweets in disagreement. Basically turns Twitter into an echochamber for those that want it to be. This isn't necessarily a BAD idea, but in many cases, the people who would utilize this are otherwise doing themselves a disservice by shutting out the arguments of others.

Add an account option to verify a unique phone number.

Phone number verification weirds me out to begin with, but becomes a bigger issue in a later suggestion (also, seems to neglect that not everyone has a phone).

Stop talking about banning IP addresses.

This is actually a legitimate point. Anyone who knows shit about computers (read: an ever-increasing number of people, particularly younger ones) knows that this is incredibly easy to bypass nowadays.

If user A has blocked user B, and user B is following user C, user B can still see any RTs of user A by user C.

As I understand this, user B can still see content from user A, despite user A blocking user B. I can actually see this as a concern.

Allow users to not show their tweets to unauthenticated users.

This seems to be a concern due to the existence of archival pages. This tactic seems to be one intended to cover up the missteps of certain individuals by not allowing said missteps to be archived, thus providing irrefutable evidence of them.

If user A has user B blocked, user B shouldn’t be able to use Twitter search to see tweets by user A.

Also a semi-fair complaint.

Allow users to block content instead of users.

This is basically an echochamber-enforcer. See my response to the first point.

Fix Tweetdeck. Fix Twitter for Android. Fix Twitter for OSX.

No comment on here, since I'm unfamiliar with Tweetdeck.

The ability to list blocked users only is useful if you’re blocking a handful of users.

If you're blocking that many users to begin with, maybe the problem isn't everyone else.

Block import/export is shit.

No comment for reasons similar to Tweetdeck.

Also,

Blocktogether reigns supreme.

Nice ad.

If someone I’ve got blocked mentions me, I don’t want to see replies to this tweet.

Another reasonably fair complaint.

Quality filter sounds rad, but let’s elaborate on what that means, and allow users to specify a sensitivity level. Here’s where things can get fun. Accounts should be scored on a variety of factors. It’s about quality of interactions. Do they often tweet at accounts that don’t tweet back? Do the majority of accounts they tweet at immediately block them? What’s their follower/following count look like? How old is their account? Did they verify their email address? Do they have a unique phone number? How many tweets have they made? Are they using the default egg profile pic? Getting even more granular, do the accounts that I follow ever interact with this user in a positive way? Do people that I follow also follow this account? Do they block this account?

Sounds like a load of BS that could be easily manipulated to me. If Twitter tried to implement such a thing, you KNOW they'd fudge it to favor the "right" people.

Allow me to see only the tweets that have been filtered.

The reasoning here is actually semi-reasonable, although at the end of the day, I can't help but feel that the people who block en masse would have issues differentiating between "actionable tweets" and disagreement.

Have a better reporting system. I should be able to view a list of all the tweets I’ve reported, along with any actions that were taken. Emails should include a link to the tweet. If you report a large number of abusive tweets, there’s no way to know which tweet is for what email. Twitter likes to ask for more information. I have no fucking clue what to tell them, because they refuse to tell me what tweet that report is even about. Even after I ask.

Again, fair enough.

If I have a protected account, people not following me can’t see my tweets. That’s great. However, they can search for my name and see tweets that other people are directing towards me.

I'm not seeing the huge issue here, honestly. This feels like more echo-chambery stuff.

Fix the API rate limits. Some of these limits — such as getting a list of followers for an account — are ridiculously low. If a user has a high number of followers and you try to pull down that list, you don’t actually have any guarantee of getting the complete follower list because you have to pause and wait for the rate limit to be refreshed.

Fair complaint.

Create an API call so I can view the users that have favorited/liked a Tweet.

Also fair.

Create an API call so I can view all the users that have RTed a tweet.

And once again, fair.

Allow me to disable Twitter moments.

I'm not familiar with Twitter moments, so no comment.

Allow users to toggle displaying tweets from blocked users in search results.

I'm not sure whether or not blocked users are shown in search results by default. If so, that's silly, and should be changed. If not, then I don't see the problem. If you blocked them, wouldn't it basically be implied that you didn't want to see anything from them in general?

If a protected user tweets at a user that isn’t following them, that user should be able to see this tweet. I shouldn’t have to follow a protected user for them to be able to interact with me.

Fair.

Allow users to only see notifications from people that are following them.

So, echo-chamber.

When I select Mentions instead of Notifications on the notifications page in Twitter web, it should remember this option.

Also fair.

tl;dr version: API stuff is reasonable, as is removing IP bans. The privacy stuff ranges from reasonable to obviously serving little more purpose than to enforce Twitter echo-chambers. Very hit and miss, and not as horrible as I would have guessed overall.

Alright, suppose I'll hit this point-by-point.

Allow users to mute all replies from a tweet.

This sort of thing would obviously be used by people who don't like it when people reply to tweets in disagreement. Basically turns Twitter into an echochamber for those that want it to be. This isn't necessarily a BAD idea, but in many cases, the people who would utilize this are otherwise doing themselves a disservice by shutting out the arguments of others.

Add an account option to verify a unique phone number.

Phone number verification weirds me out to begin with, but becomes a bigger issue in a later suggestion (also, seems to neglect that not everyone has a phone).

Stop talking about banning IP addresses.

This is actually a legitimate point. Anyone who knows shit about computers (read: an ever-increasing number of people, particularly younger ones) knows that this is incredibly easy to bypass nowadays.

If user A has blocked user B, and user B is following user C, user B can still see any RTs of user A by user C.

As I understand this, user B can still see content from user A, despite user A blocking user B. I can actually see this as a concern.

Allow users to not show their tweets to unauthenticated users.

This seems to be a concern due to the existence of archival pages. This tactic seems to be one intended to cover up the missteps of certain individuals by not allowing said missteps to be archived, thus providing irrefutable evidence of them.

If user A has user B blocked, user B shouldn’t be able to use Twitter search to see tweets by user A.

Also a semi-fair complaint.

Allow users to block content instead of users.

This is basically an echochamber-enforcer. See my response to the first point.

Fix Tweetdeck. Fix Twitter for Android. Fix Twitter for OSX.

No comment on here, since I'm unfamiliar with Tweetdeck.

The ability to list blocked users only is useful if you’re blocking a handful of users.

If you're blocking that many users to begin with, maybe the problem isn't everyone else.

Block import/export is shit.

No comment for reasons similar to Tweetdeck.

Also,

Blocktogether reigns supreme.

Nice ad.

If someone I’ve got blocked mentions me, I don’t want to see replies to this tweet.

Another reasonably fair complaint.

Quality filter sounds rad, but let’s elaborate on what that means, and allow users to specify a sensitivity level. Here’s where things can get fun. Accounts should be scored on a variety of factors. It’s about quality of interactions. Do they often tweet at accounts that don’t tweet back? Do the majority of accounts they tweet at immediately block them? What’s their follower/following count look like? How old is their account? Did they verify their email address? Do they have a unique phone number? How many tweets have they made? Are they using the default egg profile pic? Getting even more granular, do the accounts that I follow ever interact with this user in a positive way? Do people that I follow also follow this account? Do they block this account?

Sounds like a load of BS that could be easily manipulated to me. If Twitter tried to implement such a thing, you KNOW they'd fudge it to favor the "right" people.

Allow me to see only the tweets that have been filtered.

The reasoning here is actually semi-reasonable, although at the end of the day, I can't help but feel that the people who block en masse would have issues differentiating between "actionable tweets" and disagreement.

Have a better reporting system. I should be able to view a list of all the tweets I’ve reported, along with any actions that were taken. Emails should include a link to the tweet. If you report a large number of abusive tweets, there’s no way to know which tweet is for what email. Twitter likes to ask for more information. I have no fucking clue what to tell them, because they refuse to tell me what tweet that report is even about. Even after I ask.

Again, fair enough.
